reminder.notes:
## Bug fixes

- **Fixed repeating reminders firing years before their start date.** A reminder set for a date in the future with a repeat rule — "check the car battery, 1 April 2029, every day" — rang the next morning, and every morning after that. The start date was read, passed to the repeat logic, and then ignored by every rule except intervals, so daily, weekly, monthly and yearly all counted from today and the chosen date only ever set the time of day.

- **Every reminder now takes over the screen, whatever its priority.** Normal reminders arrived as a quiet notification in the tray that was easy to miss entirely — and a missed reminder is indistinguishable from a broken one. Priority now decides how insistent the alert is and whether it survives quiet hours, never whether you are interrupted at all.

  This needed the notification channel to be recreated. Android fixes a channel's importance when it first makes it and ignores every later change, so raising it in the app alone would have shipped a fix that did nothing on any phone that already had Reminder installed.

- **Location reminders now leave a trace in the diagnostics log.** Every other part of the app records what it did — scheduling, syncing, alarms, the watchdog — and geofencing recorded nothing, so "location reminders don't work" produced a log in which location was the one thing invisible. It now says whether a place was registered, or refused for want of "Allow all the time" location, or rejected by Play services and why.

## Features

- **New app icon.** The old one was a six-colour gradient bell on a white tile: nothing held its shape at the size a launcher actually draws, and the white tile disappeared into light wallpapers. It is now a single bell on the app's indigo, legible small.

## Notes

- If location reminders are not firing, the usual cause is Location permission set to "While using the app". Android will not deliver a place alert without **Allow all the time**, and the app refuses to save a location reminder without it rather than creating one that silently never fires.

mirrordrive.notes:
# Mirror v0.15.0

### Features
- App renamed "Mirror" (from "MirrorDrive"/"Mirror Drive") in the launcher, app title, and app-store listing. Package id and OAuth client are unchanged, so this update installs normally over the existing app.
- Mapping backup now lives in Drive's hidden App Data folder, one file per device install, so the same Google account signed into two phones can no longer have one phone's auto-backup silently overwrite the other's saved mappings.
- A restore picker (Settings, or offered automatically right after a fresh sign-in with no local mappings) lists every device's backup under the account and lets you choose which one to restore.
- Mapping backup now saves automatically on every add/edit/delete, not just when manually tapping "Back up" in Settings.
- Optional fleet diagnostics reporting (Settings > Troubleshooting): sends sanitized failure and background-sync delivery signals to help diagnose device-specific issues remotely. Off by default; never sends mapping paths, file names, or account details.
- Removed the "beta" label from the app-store listing and the in-app sign-in screen.

### Bug fixes
- Google Sign-In on release builds no longer fails right after install (the v0.14.0 signing-key rotation needed its new SHA-1 registered on the OAuth client; done).
- Mapping backups now actually persist across an uninstall/reinstall. Previously the backup/restore mechanism existed but was never triggered automatically, so a reinstall lost every mapping.

family.notes:
## Bug fixes

- **Fixed the app being told there was no update when there was one.** The list of published versions is cached for ten minutes by the network it comes from, and the app was reading whichever copy it was handed. So for at least ten minutes after a release — and longer if a phone or network held the file — checking for updates confidently reported that the current version was the newest. The app now always asks for a fresh copy.

  An update check that answers wrongly is worse than one that does not run: it stops you looking.

taashclub.notes:
Taash Club 1.4.1 - Card sounds that actually play, and a way to prove it

Card sounds were not playing on a real phone. Everything that could be checked
from a desk looked correct: the samples were in the APK, the audio plugin was in
the build, the files were valid 16-bit PCM, and roughly fifty call sites fired at
the right moments. The fault was in how the effects were played, and it was
invisible because every failure ended in an empty catch block.

### Features

- Awaaz sheet ab "Test" button deta hai. Ek tap, saari awaazein bajti hain, aur
  agar koi nahi baji to naam ke saath batata hai ki kaunsi. "Koi awaaz nahi aa
  rahi" ab ek aisi report hai jispe kaam ho sakta hai.
- Audio failures are reported instead of swallowed. The sound sheet shows the
  most recent one, and it is written to the device log.

### Bug fixes

- Card sounds now play through the low-latency path, which is SoundPool on
  Android. The default mode builds and prepares a media player for every single
  play; for four-to-thirty kilobyte blips fired as fast as cards are tapped that
  is both slow and unreliable, and when it fails the sound simply never arrives.
  Table music stays on the streaming path, which is the only one that can loop a
  half-megabyte track.
- Every effect is loaded once at startup rather than at the moment it is needed.
  Preparing a sample when it is first required is what made the first card of
  each game silent.
- The audio context is set once, globally, before any player exists. Previously
  only the music player carried one, so the effect players ran under whatever the
  plugin defaulted to and the two competed for audio focus.
- Playing an effect no longer calls stop() on a player that has never been given
  a source. If that threw, the empty catch swallowed it and the sound was lost.
- Effect volume raised from 0.75 to 0.9. The samples are short and were sitting
  under the table music.

### Notes

Audio sample integrity is now covered by tests: every sound in the enum must
exist, be over a kilobyte, and be 16-bit mono PCM that Android can decode. A
missing or malformed sample fails the build instead of shipping as silence.
